T: Po-tay-toes. Boil them, mash them, stick them in a stew.
D: The fellowship is broken and the war for Middle-earth begins in earnest.
P: Serve the stew when Sam cooks the rabbits in Ithilien.
S: boil them, mash them, stick them in a stew
Floury potatoes boiled until soft, mashed with lots of butter, hot milk and salt, served in a big bowl with chives.
Merry and Pippin find the stores at Isengard
Pork belly slices cured with salt and sugar overnight, rinsed, roasted at 220C until crisp, with crusty bread and pickles.
Oatcakes of oats, butter, honey and salt baked at 180C for 20 minutes, with sharp cheese and apples.
M: the stew Sam makes in Ithilien, with taters
Rabbit or chicken thighs browned, onion, carrot and thyme, stock and a splash of ale, potatoes added, simmered 90 minutes until tender.
the golden mead hall at Edoras
Lamb leg studded with garlic and rosemary, roasted at 180C to 58C, rested, with roast root vegetables and a mint and honey sauce.
W: one small bite is enough to fill a grown man
Rich shortbread squares wrapped in a leaf, the closest thing to Elvish waybread. Beat 250g butter with 100g sugar and 2 tbsp honey, then mix in 350g plain flour and a pinch of salt.
K: the drink in the great hall
Honey dissolved in warm cloudy apple juice with cinnamon and clove, served warm, or a glass of real mead.

s.note: boil them, mash them, stick them in a stew
s.how: Boil 1kg floury potatoes until soft. Mash with 80g butter, 150ml hot milk and fine salt until smooth. Pile into a big bowl and scatter with chives. Boil them, mash them, and leave the stew for later.

Melt 60g butter with 2 tbsp honey and stir into 200g rolled oats with a pinch of salt. Press thin into a lined tray and bake at 180C for 20 minutes. Cut while warm. Serve with 200g sharp cheddar and sliced apples.

m.note: the stew Sam makes in Ithilien, with taters
m.how: Brown 1kg rabbit pieces or chicken thighs. Add 2 onions, 3 carrots and thyme, then 200ml ale and 500ml stock and 600g potatoes. Simmer covered for 90 minutes until tender.

w.note: one small bite is enough to fill a grown man
w.how: Beat 250g butter with 100g sugar and 2 tbsp honey, then mix in 350g plain flour and a pinch of salt. Press 1cm thick into a tray, score into squares and bake at 160C for 30 minutes. Cut while warm and wrap each in a clean leaf or baking paper.

d.note: the drink in the great hall
d.how: Warm 1L cloudy apple juice with 3 tbsp honey, a cinnamon stick and 4 cloves for 10 minutes. Strain into mugs. For the grown-ups, pour a glass of real mead instead.
